findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses pub String fields (status, id) and pub bools (is_validated, is_sent) that allow any state combination including illegal ones (e.g., is_sent=true without sent_at_epoch_ms, is_validated=false with status="sent", multiple lifecycle flags set simultaneously).
findings.failure_mode: External code can construct or mutate PacketWorkflow into states that violate domain invariants. No constructor enforces ordering rules, so a packet could be marked sent before validation, or sent without a timestamp, or have contradictory status/is_sent pairs.
findings.fix: Replace String status and bool flags with a single typed enum or typestate that encodes valid lifecycle transitions. Use a fallible constructor that enforces invariant (is_sent requires sent_at_epoch_ms). Make all fields private.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are primitive lifecycle flags. Two separate bools cannot enforce ordering (validated before sent) or mutual exclusion.
findings.failure_mode: The boolean pair allows 4 states but only 3 are valid (not_validated, validated, validated+sent). The all-false state is ambiguous (is the packet created? failed?), and there is no way to distinguish validated-but-not-yet-sent from never-validated.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single PacketStatus enum: { Created, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive string instead of a domain enum. Any arbitrary string value is allowed.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any value ("SENT", "sent", "pending", "", "deleted") with no domain validation. The status field becomes redundant with is_sent and is_validated since there is no single source of truth.
findings.fix: Replace String status with a PacketStatus enum. The enum variants carry the domain meaning; eliminate the separate is_sent/is_validated bools.

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true without checking is_validated. No precondition enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can be marked sent without ever being validated, violating the domain invariant that only validated packets get sent. This allows data corruption — unvalidated data could leave the system.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible method on the typestate enum that returns Err(UnvalidatedPacket) when called on a non-validated state. The method should produce a Sent variant carrying sent_at_epoch_ms.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is stored alongside separate is_sent bool, meaning the timestamp can exist without is_sent=true, or is_sent=true without a timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: The invariant "is_sent implies sent_at_epoch_ms is Some" is not enforced by the type system. A packet could have a timestamp but not be marked sent (leak), or be marked sent with a None timestamp (missing audit trail).
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent enum variant so it is only present when the packet is in the Sent state. This makes the invariant structurally enforced.

findings.problem: All fields on PacketWorkflow are pub, allowing direct mutation from any crate caller.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can do PacketWorkflow { .. }.is_sent = true; or .is_validated = false; bypassing mark_sent entirely. This completely undermines the intended lifecycle discipline.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Expose lifecycle transitions only through methods or enum variants that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes PacketWorkflow by value and returns PacketWorkflow, mutating it in place with String::to_string. No separation of pure domain logic from imperative actions.
findings.failure_mode: The function is an imperative mutation, not a pure state transition. There is no immutable-by-construction domain type, making it impossible to reason about state invariants through the type system alone.
findings.fix: Define a pure PacketStatus enum with a transition method: fn validated(self) -> PacketStatus, fn sent(self) -> Result<Sent, TransitionError>. The pure core returns a new state; shell code handles any I/O like clock reads.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance claim. The crate has no test harness at all.
findings.failure_mode: Without tests or benchmarks, there is no evidence that the code behaves correctly or meets performance requirements. Changes can silently break behavior.
findings.fix: Add behavior tests covering all valid state transitions and rejected illegal transitions. Add a benchmark if performance claims exist.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive string instead of a typed newtype like PacketId.
findings.failure_mode: Any String can be used as a packet ID. There is no domain guarantee that the id is well-formed, non-empty, or unique. It could be confused with other string identifiers in the system.
findings.fix: Replace with pub(crate) struct PacketId(String) or a non-empty string newtype with a fallible constructor that validates the id format.

missing_evidence: no behavior tests for state transitions
no benchmark for mark_sent or any performance claim
no allocation analysis (String::to_string allocation in mark_sent)
no second-ring evidence (no integration tests or contract tests)
residual_risk: The PacketWorkflow struct has no type-enforced invariants. Any combination of (status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) is constructable, meaning illegal states are representable and directly constructible by callers. The mark_sent function has no precondition checks. This is a foundational architecture violation that cannot be patched with local changes — the entire type must be replaced with a typed state machine.
